title: The Explore-Exploit Tradeoff
description: About balancing exploration and exploitation in reinforcement learning, and how to manage it
content:
**The explore-exploit tradeoff** is a fundamental concept in machine learning (more specifically, reinforcement learning). It describes the dilemma an agent faces when deciding between two competing strategies:

• Exploitation - choosing the best option based on current knowledge, to maximize the immediate reward.
• Exploration - trying out new options that may lead to better outcomes in the future, at the expense of the exploitation opportunity.

Why the balance matters:
• An agent that only exploits may lock onto a suboptimal choice and never discover a better alternative.
• An agent that only explores constantly gathers new information but never uses what it has learned to gain rewards.
• Good decision-making requires combining both: using what is already known while still leaving room to discover something better.

**The epsilon-greedy algorithm** is a method used in reinforcement learning and decision-making processes to balance exploration and exploitation.

How it works:
• Most of the time (with probability 1 − ε), the agent chooses the best known action - exploitation.
• Occasionally (with probability ε), the agent selects a random action - exploration - to discover potentially better options.

The epsilon (ε) parameter controls the balance between the two:
• Higher epsilon -> more exploration.
• Lower epsilon -> more exploitation.
• ε = 0 means pure exploitation (always the best known action); ε = 1 means pure exploration (always a random action).
• In practice, epsilon is usually set to a small value (e.g., 0.1, meaning 10% of actions are random) and is often gradually decreased over time, so the agent explores early and exploits later.
